City AttorneVs Impartial Analysis of Measure
The City of San Mateo currently imposes a transactions and use tax, commonly known as a sales tax, of
it would increase this tax from 0.25% to 0.50%. A 0.25%
0.25%. If voters approve Measure
increase amounts to an extra 25 cents per $100 purchased. The additional 0.25% sales tax would
remain in effect until voters end it. Measure will be adopted if approved by a majority of voters
voting on it.
If voters approve it, the proposed tax is estimated to generate approximately $7 million a year in
locally controlled funding. Measure would be a general tax, which means that the tax revenue
could be spent for any City purpose, which includes maintenance of local streets, parks, and other
infrastructure, as well as police, fire, paramedic, crime prevention, 9-1-1 emergency response, and
traffic safety improvements. The tax would not apply to groceries or prescription medication, among
other exceptions provided by state law.
Under state law, the combined rate of all such taxes imposed by the City and San Mateo County is
capped at 2%, and there is remaining capacity within this cap of one-quarter percent (0.25%). The City
is authorized to impose this tax with voter approval. On July 20, 2026, the San Mateo City Council
voted to place Measure on the ballot.
The State would collect tax revenue under a contract with the City, and pay it to the City. Measure
would require an annual audit and provide for a committee of five members of the public to review
and report on receipts and spending of tax proceeds.
If voters approve it, the tax would be collected starting with the first day of the calendar quarter
starting 110 days after the City Council certifies election results.
A YES vote approves the measure.
Prasanna W. Rasiah
City Attorney
